summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for a left total knee arthroplasty due to severe osteoarthritis. The surgery was performed successfully, and she tolerated the procedure well. Postoperatively, she developed mild anemia with a hematocrit drop to 25% on postoperative day 4, requiring a partial red blood cell transfusion of 1.25 units, after which her levels improved to 29.7%. Pain was managed initially with a PCA pump, then transitioned to oral medications including morphine and acetaminophen. She began physical therapy on postoperative day 1, was ambulating with a walker, and voiding independently after Foley removal on day 2. Her wound healed well with no signs of infection. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with instructions on anticoagulation, wound care, activity, and follow-up. Her chronic conditions, including asthma, hypertension, and rheumatoid arthritis, were managed throughout the stay without complication.
problems: Osteoarthrosis, localized, not specified whether primary or secondary, lower leg
